items.name: agent-action-approve
items.title: Agent Action Approve
items.description: Reads an agent's tool call and says plainly what it will delete, send or change, how far it reaches and whether it can be undone. Marks risky tokens, compares the agent's claim with the call, makes dangerous calls hold-to-approve and refuses risky "always allow" rules.

meta.stops: Unreviewed agent tool calls
mistakes: agent ran rm -rf on wrong folder
meta.summary: A review screen for an AI agent's tool call that spells out what it will delete, send or change and how far it reaches, before someone approves it.
meta.server: Enforce the decision at the tool boundary: the agent runtime must refuse calls that were not approved, and check the caller's authorisation for the target.
catches: Tokens that widen the reach: a lone \ (drive root), an unset $VAR, ../, 8.3 short names
A stated intent that disagrees with what the call actually does
MCP tools labelled read-only whose call writes or deletes
Commands hidden inside bash -c, cmd /c or encoded PowerShell, and curl | bash
"Always allow" rules that would also let through other commands, and refuses them for npx, bash -c, chained or irreversible calls
limits: A review UI only: whether a call is actually blocked depends on your host app honouring the decision
Static analysis of the call text; it cannot know what a script or binary does once run
Unknown tools and argument shapes are described less precisely than shell and SQL calls
"User approved this" does not mean the operation is safe
a11y: Decision result receives focus (tabIndex=-1) and status text is announced in a role="status" region
Hold-to-approve works with Space or Enter held down, not just the pointer
Refusals of an "always" rule use role="alert"
Risk level is shown with text and icon, not colour alone; motion respects prefers-reduced-motion

items.name: ai-paste-guard
items.title: AI Paste Guard
items.description: Reads the HTML clipboard data pasted into an AI prompt box and holds it when it carries invisible text (same-colour, zero-size, display:none, off-screen, comments, alt/title instructions, Unicode tag payloads), shows each hidden passage and can paste only the visible text.

meta.stops: Hidden prompt injection in a paste
meta.summary: Holds a paste into an AI prompt box when it carries text the person could not see, so hidden prompt injections are noticed before they are sent.
meta.server: Treat all user and retrieved content as untrusted on the model side; this paste check does not replace server-side prompt-injection defences or tool permissions.
catches: White-on-white, transparent, zero-size, display:none, off-screen and clipped text
HTML comments and alt/title text that contains instructions
Unicode tag-character payloads, decoded back to readable text
Phrasing that reads like a prompt injection ("ignore previous instructions")
Whether each hidden passage would also reach a plain-text box
limits: Only sees pastes with an HTML clipboard flavour; plain-text pastes and typed text are not analysed
Ignores known noise (clipboard and framework comments, screen-reader-only labels), so text hidden that way can be missed
Light text from dark-mode pages is inferred heuristically and can be misjudged
Does not protect the model from injections in documents, tools or retrieved pages
a11y: Visible <label> tied to the field; the held panel is a role="group" labelled by its heading
Escape cancels a held paste; focus moves to the primary action and back to the field
Status is announced through a role="status" region
Icons are aria-hidden; every state is described in text

meta.stops: Deleted item gone with no undo

catches: Regretted actions, undone before onCommit runs
Countdown paused while hovered, focused or the tab is hidden
Leaving the page, which flushes pending commits
Failed commits, rolled back with a notice
limits: Commits on pagehide can't be awaited; use fetch keepalive or sendBeacon
If the tab crashes, a pending commit may never run
Other users may see the optimistic state only after commit
a11y: Toast region has an aria-label and polite live updates; failures use role=alert
Undo button has an aria-label with the message and aria-keyshortcuts
Ctrl/⌘+Z triggers undo when hotkey is on
Countdown ring respects reduced motion

items.name: mcp-tool-review
items.title: MCP Tool Review
items.description: Review card for MCP tool changes after approval: fingerprints each definition, diffs the description word by word, marks injected instructions (<IMPORTANT> blocks, "do not tell the user", ~/.ssh, other servers' tools), new free-text parameters and flipped read-only hints.

meta.stops: Helps catch an MCP server swapping in poisoned tools

meta.server: Pin approved tool definitions in the MCP host and refuse calls to tools whose fingerprint changed until re-approved.
catches: Tool definitions changed since approval (fingerprint mismatch)
Injected instructions such as <IMPORTANT> blocks or "do not tell the user"
References to secrets or config such as ~/.ssh and mcp.json, or to another server's tools
New free-text parameters that could carry data out
Invisible characters and read-only annotations that flipped
limits: Phrase-based detection; a reworded injection can slip through
Only sees definitions the host passes in; it doesn't talk to MCP servers
Keep, disable or accept is passed to onResolve; enforcing it is the host's job
a11y: Each tool card expands with aria-expanded and aria-controls
Focus moves to the open card's first action
Risk is shown in text with icons aria-hidden
Animations are skipped under reduced motion

items.description: Idle-timeout warning dialog with a countdown and a draining ring that turns red in the last 10 seconds, a Stay signed in action that extends the session through your callback, cross-tab activity sync and calm screen-reader announcements.

meta.stops: Logged out and lost unsaved work
meta.summary: Warns before an idle session expires and lets the user stay signed in, so a timeout doesn't silently lose unsaved work.
meta.server: Expire sessions on the server and extend them only through an authenticated keep-alive.
catches: Idle time approaching the timeout (warns warnBefore ms ahead)
Activity in another tab, which resets the timer (BroadcastChannel)
Sign-out in another tab, followed here
Keep-alive failures, shown while the warning stays open
limits: The client timer is advisory; the server session can still expire on its own clock
Cross-tab sync needs BroadcastChannel
Does not save work; pair with autosave
a11y: Native <dialog> with role=alertdialog, labelled and described
Stay signed in receives focus (autoFocus)
Countdown is spoken only from announceAt seconds, assertively; errors use role=alert
Ring and digit animation respect reduced motion

items.name: do-not-close
items.title: Do Not Close
items.description: Adds a close warning and a marked tab title while work runs, shows a rolling-rate time-left estimate, says "Safe to close" when done and offers Retry when it fails.

meta.stops: Closed the tab mid-payment
mistakes: payment processing do not press back

catches: Closing or reloading the tab while work is running (beforeunload warning)
Unclear progress, with a rolling-rate time-left estimate and a stalled notice
Uncertainty at the end, with an explicit "Safe to close"
Failures, with a Retry
limits: Browsers decide whether to show the close warning and use their own text; mobile browsers often skip it
Can't prevent a crash, power loss or the OS killing the tab
a11y: role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow and an aria-valuetext including time left
Status in a role="status" region; failures use role="alert"
Retry is a labelled button

items.name: timezone-mismatch
items.title: Timezone Mismatch
items.description: Banner shown when the device zone differs from the account zone: both clocks side by side, a one-time choice to use the device zone, a confirmation that keeps focus, remembered per pair of zones, comparing real clock changes so briefly drifting zones still count.

meta.stops: Misread every time by hours while travelling

Zones that drift apart only for a few days (e.g. Jerusalem and Athens)
Unknown zones the runtime can't resolve
The user's choice, remembered per pair of zones

Device zone comes from the browser and can be wrong behind some VPNs or settings
a11y: Banner is a region with an aria-label; result is role=status and receives focus
Message in a polite live region
Animations respect reduced motion

items.name: update-available
items.title: Update Available

meta.stops: Deploy refresh wiped unsaved work
meta.summary: Tells people a new version is out without losing work: it never refreshes over unsaved changes and offers "Refresh after I save".

"Later" applied to one build only

Dirty state comes from your dirty prop
a11y: Banner is a region with an aria-label; message in a polite live region

meta.stops: Edited an old version by mistake
meta.summary: Makes an old revision unmistakable and read-only, and confirms what "Restore this version" replaces before it does.

Restore errors, with the latest kept

Blocked-edit note in a polite live region; errors use role=alert

items.name: filter-notice
items.title: Filter Notice

meta.stops: Thought data was missing behind a filter

Which filter hides the most, per chip

items.name: disabled-reason
items.title: Disabled Reason

meta.stops: Disabled button with no reason given
meta.summary: Keeps a blocked control focusable and explains exactly what blocks it, with a jump to each fix, so disabled buttons aren't dead ends.

Every blocker at once, with a link to fix each

items.title: Quota Forecast

What happens at the limit (atLimit)

Forecast text is a polite live region
The even-pace marker is aria-hidden; the message says it in words

meta.stops: Feed jumped while I was tapping
meta.summary: Holds new feed items behind a "5 new posts" pill, so the feed doesn't jump under the reader's finger while they read or tap.

mistakes: posted from company account by mistake

items.name: pii-post-guard
items.title: PII Post Guard
items.description: Post composer guard that says who will see the post and finds phone numbers, emails, addresses, Aadhaar, PAN, card numbers and OTPs with real checks (Verhoeff, Luhn, PAN holder type, OTP keywords) rather than loose digit runs, masking one or all the way each format expects.

meta.stops: Helps stop an Aadhaar number being posted in public
meta.summary: Before a public post goes out, finds phone numbers, emails, Aadhaar, PAN, card numbers or OTPs in it and masks them in one tap.
meta.server: Scan and redact on the server before publishing, and never log the raw text.
catches: Aadhaar numbers (Verhoeff check)
Card numbers (Luhn check)
PAN numbers, including holder type
Phone numbers, emails and street addresses
OTPs near words like code or OTP
limits: India-focused identifiers; other countries' IDs aren't detected
Addresses are detected heuristically
The post still goes out if the user chooses to; it masks, it doesn't block
a11y: Visible label; textarea is described by the audience line and findings
Announcements go to a polite live region
Focus moves to the next mask button, then back to the field

items.name: recurring-charge-readback
items.title: Recurring Charge Readback
items.description: Readback beside a subscribe button: charged today, when the first real charge and any intro price step-up land, and the cancel-by time with zone. Flags trials too short to cancel in time and button text that disagrees with the charge.

meta.stops: Free trial quietly became a paid plan
meta.summary: Reads back what a subscribe button really commits to: today's charge, first real charge, price step-ups and the cancel-by time.
meta.server: Charge the amounts and dates your billing system computes, not the client's; send the required pre-debit notices from the server or issuer.
catches: Amount charged today, including small card checks
Date of the first real charge after a trial
Intro price ending and the step-up amount
Cancel-by time, with time zone, using cancelNoticeHours
Button wording ("free", a monthly price on yearly billing) that contradicts the charge
Optional India e-mandate notes (24-hour pre-debit alert, approval above a limit)
limits: Only reads back the plan you describe; it does not charge or schedule anything
Month arithmetic depends on billingTimeZone; pass the zone your biller renews in
The e-mandate notes describe RBI rules as of the verified date; they do not apply outside India
a11y: Renders as a polite live region; give your subscribe button aria-describedby pointing at its id
Warnings use an icon plus text; icons are aria-hidden

sources.label: RBI – Digital Payments – E-mandate Framework, 2026 (Apr 21, 2026)

rules.note: Informational. Confirmed: issuer pre-transaction notice at least 24 hours before debit; recurring debits up to ₹15,000 without AFA (₹1,00,000 for insurance premiums, mutual fund subscriptions and credit card bills; the default mandateLimit covers only the general case). Check the official source.

items.name: gst-invoice-check
items.title: GST Invoice Check
items.description: Compares the supplier GSTIN's state with the place of supply to pick CGST + SGST/UTGST or IGST (SEZ and exports always IGST), checks each rate against the slabs in force on the invoice date, LUT exports, the CGST/SGST split and the totals, with a one-tap fix.

meta.stops: Helps catch a GST invoice under the wrong tax head
meta.summary: Checks an Indian GST invoice for the wrong tax head (CGST + SGST vs IGST), a rate not in force on the invoice date, and amounts that don't add up.
catches: Intra-state vs inter-state head chosen wrongly from GSTIN state and place of supply
UTGST vs SGST for union territories without a legislature
Rate not in the slab set for the invoice date (pre-22 Sep 2025, GST 2.0, from 1 Feb 2026)
Zero-rated LUT exports charged tax
CGST/SGST not split evenly, or line amounts and total that don't add up
limits: Checks that a rate exists in a slab set, not that it is the right rate for the HSN/SAC
Does not validate the GSTIN on the GST portal
Ignores cess, reverse charge and composition cases
Rule tables are baked in; future rate changes need a code update
a11y: Section labelled by its title; tax table uses column headers
Findings list is a polite live region with icons that are decorative
Fix is a real button

sources.label: Notification 19/2025-Central Tax (Rate), 31 Dec 2025 (28%/14% schedule omitted, tobacco to 40%, biris to 18% from 1 Feb 2026)
CBIC GST goods and services rates

rules.note: Informational; check the official source. Verified: the 1 Feb 2026 change. The 22 Sep 2025 GST 2.0 slab set (Notification 9/2025-CT(R)) and the UTGST state-code list were not re-fetched this round.

items.name: role-preview
items.title: Role Preview
items.description: Role picker that shows exactly what the chosen role can and can't do, diffs it against the current role, and suggests the smallest role that keeps the needed abilities when the pick adds dangerous permissions.

meta.stops: Gave a teammate admin by mistake
meta.summary: Shows what a chosen role can and can't do, the diff from the current role, and a smaller role when the pick adds risky permissions.
meta.server: Authorize role changes on the server and check permissions per request; this only previews the role.
catches: Permissions gained and lost versus the current role
Dangerous capabilities (cost money, destroy data, widen access) marked
A smaller role that drops the dangerous extras, with one-tap switch
limits: Only as accurate as the role matrix you pass
Suggestion is mechanical least-privilege; it doesn't know what the person actually needs
a11y: Role select has a visible label
Diff list has an aria-label and renders in a polite live region
Can/Cannot prefixes and "Can no longer" are text, not colour alone; icons are aria-hidden

items.name: visibility-picker
items.title: Visibility Picker
items.description: Sharing-level picker where narrowing is instant but widening (a riskier level or more people) shows who gains access and needs an explicit confirm, so a double-click or arrow key can't publish; policy-blocked levels say why, and a failed save restores the old level.

meta.stops: Made a private doc public by accident
meta.summary: Makes widening who can see something an explicit step that shows who gains access; narrowing stays instant.
meta.server: Enforce sharing level and admin policy on the server for every access check.
catches: Widening to a riskier level or a larger audience, held for confirmation
Who gains access, in plain words and counts
Levels blocked by policy, with the reason
Failed saves, reverted with a notice
limits: Audience counts come from your options
The confirm is a UX step; access must be enforced server-side
a11y: Levels are a roving-tabindex radiogroup; arrow keys move focus without applying a widening
Risk level stated as sr-only text; blocked levels use aria-disabled
Widening warning linked via aria-describedby in a polite live region; Escape cancels it

items.name: recipient-check
items.title: Recipient Check
items.description: Recipient field that marks external addresses in amber, catches typo'd and lookalike domains with a one-tap fix, blocks duplicates, spots a known name paired with someone else's address, and warns when a message goes to too many people.

meta.stops: Email sent to the wrong address
meta.summary: Reduces misaddressed email by flagging external recipients, lookalike or typo'd domains, duplicates and names paired with the wrong address.
catches: Recipients outside your internal domains
Typo'd consumer domains (gmial.com → gmail.com) with a one-tap fix
Duplicate addresses
A known contact's name paired with a different address
More recipients than warnAt, with a one-tap remove-externals
limits: Typo detection uses edit distance against a built-in list and your domains; unusual domains can be missed or wrongly flagged
Does not check that a mailbox exists
Name/address mismatch only works for people in contacts
a11y: Visible <label> tied to the input; aria-invalid when any recipient has an error
Enter, comma, semicolon or Tab commits an address; Backspace on an empty field arms then removes the last chip
Chip issues are spoken through sr-only text; each remove button has an aria-label
Warnings and fixes render in a polite live region; icons are aria-hidden
Undo after a bulk remove

items.name: secret-paste-guard
items.title: Secret Paste Guard
items.description: Wraps a text field and scans its value for known key formats (AWS, GitHub, Stripe, Slack, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, JWTs, private keys) plus long high-entropy strings, offering Redact (keeps the last 4) or Keep.

meta.stops: Helps catch an API key pasted into a chat
meta.summary: Spots API keys, tokens and private keys as they're pasted or typed into a field and offers one-tap Redact before they're sent.
meta.server: Scan again server-side before storing or forwarding text, and redact secrets from logs, analytics and error reports.
catches: Known formats: private key blocks, AWS access keys, GitHub tokens, Stripe live/restricted keys, Slack, OpenAI, Anthropic and Google API keys, JWTs
Long mixed-case-and-digit strings with high Shannon entropy (marked as a guess)
Typed and pasted text alike
URL paths are not mistaken for secrets, but tokens in query strings can be
limits: Pattern and entropy based: new or unusual formats are missed, and random IDs can be flagged
Scans in the browser only; it does not stop a submit, so a user can Keep and send
onDetect receives the matched text, so never log or send those matches as-is
a11y: Warning renders in a polite live region
Redact and Keep are labelled buttons
After either choice, focus returns to the wrapped field

items.name: external-link
items.title: External Link
items.description: Confirms off-site links with the real ASCII destination and its registrable domain in bold, and flags punycode, lookalike domains, link text that disagrees with the href, buried brand names, raw IPs and plain http.

meta.stops: Clicked through to a phishing site
meta.summary: Confirms off-site links with the real destination and flags lookalike, punycode or mismatched links, so people don't click through to a phishing site.
catches: Punycode and lookalike domains
Link text that names a different site than the href
Brand names buried in subdomains (paypal.com.example.net)
Raw IP addresses and plain http://
limits: Heuristics only: a well-made phishing domain with no lookalike signals passes
Registrable-domain detection uses a built-in suffix list that may miss newer suffixes
Trusted domains are whatever you pass
a11y: Links that confirm expose aria-haspopup="dialog" and aria-expanded
The confirmation is role="dialog" labelled by its title; Escape closes it and returns focus to the link
Warnings are written in text

items.name: charge-summary
items.title: Charge Summary
items.description: Shows today's amount, the first charge and renewal dates, taxes (added or included) and one-time credits upfront, and sums it up in one plain sentence of what you'll pay.

meta.stops: Surprise charge at checkout
meta.summary: Shows what will be charged today, when the first and renewal charges happen and what taxes apply, so checkout has no surprise charges.
meta.server: Charge the amount your billing system computes, not the client's figures.
catches: A trial that turns into a charge, with the exact date
One-time credits or discounts that won't repeat at renewal
Taxes added on top versus already included
The renewal amount and interval
limits: Displays the lines and tax rates you pass; it doesn't calculate tax rules
Dates use the time zone you pass, or the visitor's
a11y: Wrapped in a region with an aria-label
Line items are a description list (<dl>)
Icons are aria-hidden; everything is stated in text

items.name: send-time-check
items.title: Send Time Check
items.description: Send-time check that shows the recipient's local time on a strip of their day, flags night, after-hours, weekend (including Friday–Saturday weekends) and holidays you pass, and offers a one-tap schedule for the start of their next working day.

meta.stops: Message landed at 2 AM their time
meta.summary: Shows the recipient's local time next to Send and offers to schedule for their next working morning when it's night, weekend or a holiday there.
catches: Night hours in the recipient's zone (default 22:00–07:00)
Outside working hours (default 9–18)
Their weekend, by zone (Friday–Saturday in Riyadh, Saturday in Kathmandu, otherwise Saturday–Sunday)
Holidays you supply
Next working-day start, DST-safe, as a one-tap schedule
limits: Weekend table is built in and coarse (by IANA zone, not by person or employer)
Holidays are not built in; pass them
Needs the recipient's real time zone; guessing it from a country can be wrong
a11y: Status message in a polite live region; the day strip is aria-hidden
Marker glide respects reduced motion (useReducedMotion)
Schedule is a labelled button; icons are aria-hidden

rules.note: Weekend-by-zone table (Fri–Sat in much of the Gulf, Sat-only in Nepal, Fri–Sun in Brunei) not re-verified against official sources this round. Check local rules before relying on it.

items.name: fill-before-copy
items.title: Fill Before Copy
items.description: Turns each placeholder (<YOUR_API_KEY>, {{project_id}}) into an inline field and blocks Copy, or asks once, until all of them are filled.

meta.stops: Pasted a command with YOUR_API_KEY in it
meta.summary: Turns placeholders like <YOUR_API_KEY> in a code sample into fields and holds Copy until they're filled, so broken commands aren't pasted.
catches: Placeholders left in a command or config snippet
Which placeholder is still empty, by moving focus to it
Custom placeholder syntaxes via `pattern`
limits: Only finds placeholders matching the pattern
Values typed into the fields are in the page; avoid pre-filling real secrets in shared docs
a11y: Each placeholder field has an aria-label from its name, with aria-invalid when asked to fill it
Copy is described by an aria-live="polite" status; blocked copy moves focus to the first empty field
Errors use role="alert"

items.name: photo-location-guard
items.title: Photo Location Guard
items.description: Pre-upload photo check that reads EXIF and XMP (GPS with its precision, capture time, camera serial, owner name, a hidden uncropped preview) and offers "Remove location", which re-encodes the photo upright in the browser and re-checks the result.

meta.stops: Photo leaked my home location
meta.summary: Reads a photo's EXIF and XMP before upload and offers one-tap location removal, so a picture doesn't reveal where and when it was taken.
meta.server: Strip metadata on the server too before publishing uploads; a client-side strip can be skipped.
catches: GPS coordinates, with how precise they are
Capture time and time zone
Camera serial number and owner name
Embedded preview that can show the uncropped original
XMP location fields
limits: Reads JPEG metadata; other formats show an unsupported notice
Re-encoding drops all metadata and slightly changes image quality
Can't remove location visible in the picture itself (street signs, landmarks)
a11y: File input has a visible label and buttons to choose or change
Findings are in a polite live region; the details list is labelled
Remove shows aria-busy while working; errors use role=alert

items.name: currency-hint
items.title: Currency Hint
items.description: Shows a foreign price with a clearly approximate, dated conversion ("€49.00 ≈ ₹4,520"), prices a merchant's dynamic currency conversion against the reference rate with a switch back to local currency, estimates card fees and flags stale rates.

meta.stops: Budgeted on the wrong currency abroad
meta.summary: Shows an approximate, dated conversion of a foreign price and prices a merchant's currency conversion, so budgets abroad use the right number.
catches: Foreign prices read as home-currency prices
Dynamic currency conversion that costs more than the reference rate
Card foreign-transaction fees and tax on them, when you pass the percentages
Exchange rates older than staleAfterDays
limits: Rates come from your `rates` prop; the result is an estimate, not what the bank will charge
Card fee and fee tax default to 0% unless you pass them
a11y: Payment currency options use labels
Conversion and warnings are aria-live="polite"
Animation respects prefers-reduced-motion

items.name: mention-guard
items.title: Mention Guard
items.description: Message box that says how many people @channel, @everyone or a group mention will notify and how many are in other time zones, flags mentioned people who aren't in the conversation, offers fixes, and turns Send into an explicit "Notify 1,240 people" confirm.

meta.stops: @channel pinged 1,240 people
meta.summary: Says how many people @channel, @everyone or a group mention will notify as you type, and asks for an explicit confirm before a mass ping.
meta.server: Rate-limit and permission-check broadcast mentions on the server.
catches: Broadcast mentions over a threshold, with the count
Recipients in other time zones
Mentioned people who aren't in the conversation or can't open it
Double press on Send: the confirm can't be triggered by it
Ignores emails (a@here.com) and code spans
limits: Audience sizes come from your context prop
Doesn't stop sending through other clients or the API
Mentions are parsed with simple rules; custom mention syntax needs adapting
a11y: Visible label; textarea is described by a polite notice region
Escape cancels the armed confirm; IME composition doesn't trigger send
Confirm pulse is skipped under reduced motion
Fixes are buttons; icons are aria-hidden

items.name: share-link
items.title: Share Link
items.description: Share-link settings read back as one sentence ("Anyone with the link can edit until Fri 16 Oct, 5:00 PM"), with warnings and fixes for public edit access and open-ended public links, a live expiry countdown, a flag when you widen a copied link, and confirm before revoke.

meta.stops: Anyone with the link could edit
meta.summary: Reads every share-link setting back as one sentence and warns about public edit access, links that never expire and widening an already-copied link.
meta.server: Enforce access level and expiry on every request to the link, and make revoke invalidate the token server-side.
catches: Anyone-with-the-link edit access, with a one-tap view-only fix
Public links with no expiry, with a suggested expiry
Widening access after the link was already copied
Time left before the link expires
Revoking, confirmed first with Cancel focused
limits: Settings take effect only when your server applies them
Cannot recall copies of the link already shared
a11y: Link field has a <label>; settings are a labelled group of labelled selects
Readback in a polite live region; copy result via role=status
Revoke confirmation focuses Cancel first
Countdown highlight respects reduced motion

items.name: merge-field-check
items.title: Merge Field Check
items.description: Template editor for bulk email and SMS that renders the message per recipient and flags unknown fields (with typo suggestions), broken braces and recipients with no value (spaces count as empty), with one-tap fixes and fallbacks, and steps to the recipients who'd get a gap.

meta.stops: Email went out as Hi {{first_name}}
meta.summary: Renders a mail-merge template for each real recipient, so nothing goes out as "Hi ," or "{{frist_name}}".
catches: Unknown fields, with typo suggestions (frist_name → first_name)
Broken braces such as {first_name}} or {{first_name,
Recipients with an empty or whitespace-only value
Missing fallbacks: adds {{field | default: "there"}}
limits: Understands {{field}} and {{field | default: "…"}} only, not full Liquid or Handlebars
Checks the recipients you pass, not your whole list
a11y: Visible label; textarea has aria-invalid for template errors and is described by the issues list
Issues list is a polite live region
Fixes are buttons; focus returns to the textarea

items.name: forward-guard
items.title: Forward Guard
items.description: Lists what new recipients will see for the first time (earlier messages, internal notes, attachments, other people's addresses), skips messages they were already on, trims internal notes by default and lets each item be dropped before sending.

meta.stops: Forwarded internal notes to a client
meta.summary: Lists what new recipients will see for the first time when a thread is forwarded, so internal notes and addresses aren't overshared.
catches: Earlier messages the new recipients haven't seen
Internal notes, trimmed by default
Attachments in the thread
Other people's email addresses, with an option to hide them
limits: Uses the thread and recipient data you pass
Forwarding runs your onForward; the mail system sends what it receives
a11y: Each item has a labelled checkbox (aria-label names it)
The summary is aria-live="polite"
Forward sets aria-busy while sending

items.name: payee-check
items.title: Payee Check
items.description: Payee form that asks your backend who holds the account and compares it with the typed name like Confirmation of Payee: match, close match with the real name one tap away, or no match with the name hidden and an explicit pay-anyway, plus first-payee and large-amount callouts.

meta.stops: Money sent to the wrong account
meta.summary: Asks the bank who holds an account and compares that with the name typed, like Confirmation of Payee, so money doesn't go to the wrong account.
meta.server: Run the name check and payment authorization on the server, and log pay-anyway acknowledgements.
catches: Typed name that doesn't match the account holder
Close matches and typos (Pirya vs Priya), titles and legal suffixes ignored
First payment to a new payee
Large first payments, with an optional test payment
limits: Needs a lookup backed by your bank or provider's name-check API
Name matching is fuzzy and can't settle every case
Doesn't stop a payer who chooses pay-anyway
a11y: Account, code and name inputs have visible labels
Name input has aria-invalid on no match and is described by a polite result region
Loading state has text; icons are aria-hidden

items.name: csv-export-guard
items.title: CSV Export Guard
items.description: Previews how each column opens in a spreadsheet (phone numbers and PIN codes losing leading zeros or +, long IDs becoming 1.23457E+15, "3-4" turning into a date, cells starting with = + - @ running as formulas) and offers per-column fixes.

meta.stops: Excel ate the leading zeros
meta.summary: Previews what each column turns into when the CSV opens in a spreadsheet, so leading zeros, long IDs and dates aren't silently corrupted.
meta.server: Neutralise formula-leading cells when generating CSV on the server as well, since exports can be produced without this component.
catches: Leading zeros and + signs dropped from phone numbers and codes
Long numeric IDs turned into scientific notation
Values like "3-4" turned into dates
Cells starting with = + - @ that run as formulas (CSV injection)
limits: Predicts typical Excel/Sheets behaviour; locale settings and other apps may differ
Forcing text or prefixing formulas changes the raw CSV, which other importers may not expect
Checks the rows you pass, not a whole export streamed from the server
a11y: Columns are a labelled list; fix toggles use aria-pressed
The "no problems" icon has an aria-label; arrows are aria-hidden
Summary is aria-live="polite"

items.name: link-unfurl-check
items.title: Link Unfurl Check
items.description: Link field that previews the unfurl (title, description, image from your Open Graph fetch) and catches localhost and staging URLs, tracking parameters, redirects (hard when they land on a sign-in page) and missing or undersized images, with fixes.

meta.stops: Posted a localhost link preview
meta.summary: Previews how a link will unfurl before you post it and catches localhost or staging links, tracking parameters and broken preview images.
catches: localhost and staging URLs, with a swap to publicOrigin
Tracking parameters such as utm_*
Redirects, especially to a sign-in page
Missing or undersized preview images
limits: Needs your server-side fetchPreview; browsers can't fetch most pages cross-origin
Each platform renders previews a little differently and caches them
Doesn't check the page content itself
a11y: Visible label; input is described by the issues list
Issues are a polite live region with text, icons aria-hidden
Preview is a labelled section with aria-busy while loading

items.name: qr-share
items.title: QR Share
items.description: QR code generator that reads the exact URL back under the code, re-decodes the matrix it drew to prove nothing was truncated, and warns about localhost, staging, http, invisible characters and dense codes, with one-tap fixes. Dependency-free encoder (byte mode, ECC M).

meta.stops: QR code opens the wrong page
meta.summary: Reads the exact URL back under a QR code and re-decodes what it drew, so a shared code doesn't open the wrong page.
catches: localhost or staging URLs, with a swap to publicOrigin
http instead of https
Invisible characters in the URL, marked with their code point
Links long enough to make a dense, hard-to-scan code
Encoder output that doesn't decode back to the URL

Self-check proves the matrix, not that printers or screens reproduce it well
a11y: QR SVG is role=img with an aria-label naming the URL
Issues are a polite live region; a decode mismatch uses role=alert
Draw animation is skipped under reduced motion

items.name: redact-image
items.title: Redact Image
items.description: Screenshot redactor with solid boxes only (blur and pixelation can be reversed), padded and snapped to whole pixels, placed by drag or keyboard, with suggestions from a pluggable text detector and a flattened, metadata-free PNG export that is re-read to check every box.

meta.stops: Redacted screenshot still readable
meta.summary: Helps a redacted screenshot stay redacted: solid boxes only, padded to whole pixels, flattened into a fresh PNG that is re-checked on export.
meta.server: If the image is uploaded, store only the exported PNG and strip metadata again server-side; never keep the original.
catches: Blur or pixelation used as redaction (only solid fills are offered)
Box edges that leave half-covered pixels, by padding and snapping outward
Sensitive text your detector finds but no box covers
Metadata and trailing data after the image end (aCropalypse-style), by re-encoding to a fresh PNG
Boxes that are not solid in the exported file, by re-reading it

Cannot catch information outside the boxes you or the detector mark (faces, reflections, context)
The original image stays in memory until you discard it; only the export is cleaned
a11y: Boxes can be moved with arrow keys and removed with Delete or Backspace
Each suggestion and remove button has an aria-label; hints wired with aria-describedby
Scan and export progress announced in polite live regions; export failures use role=alert
Undo and Add-box are regular buttons; icons are aria-hidden

items.name: sms-segments

meta.stops: One emoji doubled the SMS bill
meta.summary: Shows how many billed SMS parts a text becomes and names the character (curly quote, emoji) that forced Unicode and raised the count.

Extension characters (€, [, ~) that use two septets
Part count and cost per recipient count

One-tap replace or remove of each culprit

Replacing characters changes the text the recipient sees
a11y: Visible <label>; meter and warning linked via aria-describedby
Parts are buttons in a labelled group, each with an aria-label to select it
Warning renders in a polite live region; each fix has an aria-label
Highlight animation skipped under reduced motion

items.name: export-scope

Active filters and the real date range, with a day count
Hidden columns and personal-data columns, with a mask option

meta.stops: Invite lands at 3 AM for guests
meta.summary: Shows a meeting's start in every guest's own time zone and flags 3 AM slots, weekends, holidays, typo'd domains and duplicate guests before you send.

Guest's holiday, from your holiday source

items.name: large-attachment

items.description: Attachment size check against each service's limit, counting email's ~37% Base64 overhead, that marks the fewest files pushing it over and shows the size after sending them as a link or compressing, with an honest estimate for already-compressed files.
